title: The subscription gateway serves sustained transport-failure windows with no rate-limit notice at all; those deaths are distinguishable from the quota wall only by observed_quota being absent, and a turn-1-gated requeue under the same frozen Revision recovers them

evidence.note: representative retry-exhaustion shape: 10/10 api_retry events with error "unknown" and null error_status spaced ~33-40 s apart, then a synthetic assistant API-error message and result is_error true; ZERO rate_limit_event anywhere in the retained stream. Twelve of the fifteen 2026-09-15 v118-c gateway deaths share this shape.

the billed-call variant: one 96-second billed assistant call, then transport death with no notice. The other two variants are streams truncated mid-retry-backoff (no terminal result line at all). The window was sustained 23:09-02:54 (2026-09-15/16); two shorter windows occurred 2026-09-14 (attempt b turn-7 retry-exhaustion, attempt f connection-lost-mid-response) and 2026-09-15 ~20:05.

the recovery leg: the -d requeue relaunched all sixteen faulted tasks under the same frozen v118 with a turn-1 gate (stop if the first task dies at turn 1). The gate passed at 06:59 and all sixteen tasks reached full campaigns with zero gateway deaths -- the window was transient, and the queue discipline (fresh-suffix workspaces, gate, sequential relaunch) recovered it without a Revision change.

observation: The F-2026-09-15-001 attribution seam made the two provider-death families legible: quota-wall streams terminate on a rejected rate-limit notice that observed_quota now reports, while gateway-transport streams carry no notice layer event at all, so observed_quota is correctly absent from their fault payloads. Fifteen of twenty-four v118-c tasks died this way in one sustained overnight window (three windows total observed on this arm), each recorded as a bare exit-code provider_fault whose only distinguishing feature is the absence of observed_quota. That absence is diagnostic but implicit -- an operator reading the fault payload cannot tell 'no notice existed' from 'the seam failed to mine one'. The -d requeue establishes the class is transient and operationally recoverable under the same frozen Revision.
proposed_change: Make the absence explicit rather than inferred: at the exit-code fault seam, when the retained stdout contains no valid rate-limit notice, record observed_quota as a named absent shape (e.g. {"observed": "no_notice"}) instead of omitting the key, keeping replay rederivation and the never-substitute rule unchanged. No change to turn admission -- a stream with no notice still fails closed where it fails today. The operational recipe (turn-1 gate plus fresh-suffix requeue, never deleting the faulted workspace) is already validated by the -d batch and needs no code.
verification_plan: Protocol seam change, so replay: rederive the absent shape from the fifteen cited v118-c gateway streams (each must report no_notice, never a fabricated earlier notice) and confirm the seventeen F-2026-09-15-001 wall streams still report their rejected notices; contract tests for the absent shape and for evidence sealed before the field.
